title: The Hollow Crown of Blackthorn

beats.goal: King Kaelen Vane claims the Blackthorn Crown at his coronation, accepting the burden of rule.
beats.conflict: The Crown's first hunger prickles against his temples — a cold, metallic pressure that tastes of old blood — while the court expects a savior-king.
beats.outcome: Kaelen wears the Crown; the hunger settles like a second heartbeat. He vows to be the ruler who breaks the cycle.

beats.goal: Kaelen investigates the Crown's history in the sealed Royal Archives, seeking proof of the curse.
beats.conflict: Master Vorys, the Court Physician, obstructs access; the archives are fragmented, censored by generations of kings. Each prior reign ends in 'sudden illness' or 'divine madness.'
beats.outcome: Kaelen finds a single intact journal: King Alaric III wrote his own transformation — teeth growing inward, memories eaten, the Crown whispering. The curse is real.

beats.goal: Kaelen rationalizes the curse, convincing himself his will and scholarship can master what destroyed his predecessors.
beats.conflict: Queen Isolde confronts him with his sleepless nights, his fingers already gilded at the tips. She demands abdication for their son Rowan's sake.
beats.outcome: Kaelen refuses. He frames the Crown as a tool — a parasite he can starve by ruling justly. The lie becomes his armor.

beats.goal: The first undeniable symptom manifests during a border dispute negotiation.
beats.conflict: Mid-parley, Kaelen's jaw unhinges slightly; a new molar, black as iron, pushes through his gum. He swallows the blood and continues speaking.
beats.outcome: The transformation has begun physically. Kaelen hides it. Duke Malric, the rival noble, notices the pause — and the blood on Kaelen's lip.

beats.goal: Kaelen faces the abdication window: he could name Rowan regent and step aside before the corruption deepens.
beats.conflict: The Crown whispers that Rowan is weak, that Malric would butcher the boy, that only Kaelen's monstrosity can protect the kingdom. Isolde pleads one last time.
beats.outcome: Kaelen refuses abdication. He chooses the Crown. The hunger surges in approval. Act One closes on his first deliberate act of corruption: ordering Vorys to falsify his health records.

beats.goal: Kaelen tests the Crown's mechanics — discovering it feeds on moral memory, not just flesh.
beats.conflict: He executes a corrupt tax collector. The Crown devours Kaelen's memory of the man's pleading children. The act feels clean. Righteous. Easy.
beats.outcome: Kaelen realizes the Crown doesn't just change his body — it edits his conscience. He begins selecting victims strategically: enemies, traitors, 'necessary' sacrifices.

beats.goal: Isolde confronts the stranger in her husband's skin; their marriage fractures.
beats.conflict: Kaelen cannot recall their wedding vow — the Crown ate it. He mimics affection perfectly. Isolde realizes the man she loves is already gone.
beats.outcome: Isolde flees to the convent-tower with Rowan. Kaelen lets them go, telling himself it's for their safety. The Crown purrs at the isolation.

beats.goal: Vorys reveals the full mechanism: the Crown houses the consciousness of all twelve prior kings, a chorus of hunger.
beats.conflict: Vorys offers a ritual to sever the Crown's hold — it requires Kaelen's voluntary death. Kaelen has Vorys imprisoned instead.
beats.outcome: The scholar silenced. The Crown's voices grow louder in Kaelen's mind — Alaric III, the Tooth-King; Mara the Bone-Weaver; others. They advise him now.

beats.goal: Duke Malric rebels, marching on the capital. Kaelen must use the Crown's power openly to survive.
beats.conflict: Malric's army outnumbers the loyalists three-to-one. The Crown offers victory — if Kaelen feeds it the lives of his own honor guard.
beats.outcome: Kaelen accepts. He leads the charge, his jaw now permanently distended, teeth like needles. He wins. The court cheers their monster-king.

beats.goal: Kaelen crosses the point of no return: he feeds the Crown a loyal innocent to save a strategic asset.
beats.conflict: The Crown demands a child's memory — the son of a general whose loyalty Kaelen needs. The general offers his own son willingly, believing it honor.
beats.outcome: Kaelen takes the boy's memory of his mother. The general's loyalty is secured. Kaelen no longer rationalizes. He feeds the Crown because it is easier than ruling without it.

beats.goal: Kaelen's monstrosity is revealed publicly during the Feast of Saint Veyra.
beats.conflict: The Crown forces a transformation mid-ceremony — Kaelen's skin splits, revealing gold-threaded muscle, teeth spilling from his cheeks like coins. He does not hide it.
beats.outcome: The court does not flee. They kneel. The kingdom has always known; they have always accepted. Blackthorn feeds its rulers to the Crown willingly.

beats.goal: Kaelen confronts the kingdom's complicity — the nobles, the priests, the people all benefit from the Crown's tyranny.
beats.conflict: Isolde returns, not to save him, but to negotiate Rowan's survival. She reveals she has known for years; the convent-tower trains heirs to wear the Crown.
beats.outcome: Kaelen realizes the tragedy: there is no victim, only participants. He is not the first to choose the Crown. He is simply the latest.

beats.goal: Rowan is brought before the throne — not as son, but as successor. The succession mechanism activates.
beats.conflict: The Crown demands the transfer. Kaelen's consciousness fights the voices of twelve kings who want to stay. Rowan, sixteen and terrified, reaches for the Crown.
beats.outcome: Kaelen guides Rowan's hand. He teaches the boy the first lie: 'You can control it.' The Crown passes. Kaelen's body collapses — hollow, human, finally dead.

beats.goal: The final surrender: Kaelen's mind joins the chorus inside the Crown, becoming the thirteenth voice.
beats.conflict: As his awareness fades, Kaelen sees through the Crown's eyes — not as king, but as hunger. He understands the Crown is not cursed. It is a mirror.
beats.outcome: Kaelen's voice settles into the gold. He will whisper to the next king. He will hunger. He is the Crown now.

beats.goal: Rowan wears the Crown. The cycle completes. The kingdom endures.
beats.conflict: Rowan's hand trembles as the cold gold settles on his brow. The hunger pricks his temples. He thinks of his mother in the tower. He thinks of his father's hollow eyes.
beats.outcome: Rowan straightens. His jaw sets. He speaks the coronation oath. The Crown doth glitter. Beneath its gold lie teeth. The hunger waits. The story begins again.

approval_basis: Runtime structural validation: title and complete chapter beats.
